biography: James "Showtime" Myers didn't grow up with a silver spoon or a legacy name. He was raised in the gritty suburbs of Chicago, where the roar of engines was more likely to come from souped-up street racers than any sanctioned track. James's racing career began almost by accident. At 16, he was helping a neighbor fix up a beat-up go-kart. One test run later, and James was hooked. The raw, unfiltered speed lit a fire in him. He began hitting local karting tracks, hustling his way into races and quickly making a name for himself with his aggressive, almost reckless driving style. He wasn't the most technically gifted, but he had an innate feel for the kart and a refusal to back down from any challenge. The Kart 2-Stroke 125cc Shifter team, a small but ambitious outfit, took a chance on him. Now, at 38, James is a veteran presence. While championships have remained elusive, his flashy driving and unwavering determination have made him a fan favorite, a testament to the fact that passion and grit can take you far, even without a trust fund or a pedigree.
drivingStyle: Myers is an aggressive, late-braking driver who thrives on chaos. He's known for pushing his equipment to the absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of control. He attacks corners with a "no lift" approach, believing that momentum is key to overtaking. While this can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also makes him prone to errors and mechanical failures. Tire management isn't exactly his strong suit; he prefers to run hard and fast, sacrificing longevity for immediate pace. Under pressure, he tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes to his detriment, but that is what his fans love about him.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles. Alvarez, with his meticulous and calculated approach, often clashes with Myers's reckless abandon. Their contrasting personalities and driving philosophies make them natural rivals.
Dubois accused Myers of blocking her during a crucial qualifying session, costing her a potential pole position. The animosity has been simmering ever since.
Myers and Tanaka have had multiple on-track collisions, often resulting in damaged karts and heated exchanges in the paddock. Their battles are always intense and unpredictable.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky wristband, a faded and tattered piece of fabric from his first karting victory.
Listens to heavy metal music at ear-splitting volume right before a race to pump himself up.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the limits and putting on a show. If you ain't sliding, you ain't trying!"
careerHighlight: Winning the Chicago Karting Grand Prix in 2018, a victory he dedicated to his late father, who introduced him to racing. He started the race in P8 but won it in spectacular fashion with a last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship-deciding race in 2021 due to a mechanical failure while leading, losing the title by a single point.
